question: Were you under age 24 at the end of 2025?
why_ask: A full-time student under 24 can be a parent's qualifying child, and age affects whether the American opportunity credit is refundable and whether the kiddie tax applies.
retrieval_query: qualifying child age test full-time student under 24
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab C, Dependents and Tab J refundable AOTC chart (structure only)

question: Did you pay more than half of your own living costs for 2025 (housing, food, tuition) from your own earnings?
why_ask: A child who provides over half of their own support is not a qualifying child; it also matters for the refundable American opportunity credit and the kiddie tax.
retrieval_query: qualifying child support test provided over half of own support

question: Were you enrolled at least half-time in a program leading to a degree or credential for at least one term that began in 2025?
why_ask: At least half-time enrollment in a degree program is required for the American opportunity credit.
retrieval_query: American opportunity credit at least half-time student degree program
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Did you receive a Form 1098-T (Tuition Statement) from your school for 2025?
why_ask: Education credits generally require Form 1098-T; it is usually in the student's online school account.
retrieval_query: Form 1098-T required to claim education credit
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Does your Form 1098-T show an amount in box 4 or box 6?
why_ask: Boxes 4 and 6 are adjustments for a prior year; Pub 4012 marks these Forms 1098-T as out of scope.
retrieval_query: Form 1098-T box 4 box 6 adjustments prior year
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Did you receive any scholarship, fellowship or grant for 2025 (for example a Pell Grant or Cal Grant)?
why_ask: Scholarships are tax free only up to qualified education expenses and reduce the expenses that count for credits.
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Was the total of your scholarships and grants more than your tuition, required fees, and required books and supplies?
why_ask: The part above qualified education expenses, or used for room and board, is taxable to the student.
retrieval_query: scholarship exceeds qualified education expenses taxable room and board
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Did any scholarship or fellowship require you to teach, do research or perform other work (for example as a TA or RA)?
why_ask: The part of a scholarship that pays for required services is taxable income, usually reported on a W-2.
retrieval_query: scholarship payment for teaching research services taxable
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: In how many earlier tax years was the American opportunity credit (or Hope credit) claimed for you, by you or your parents?
why_ask: The American opportunity credit can be claimed for a student for at most 4 tax years.
retrieval_query: American opportunity credit claimed for only four tax years
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Had you completed the first four years of college before 2025 began?
why_ask: The American opportunity credit is only for the first four years of postsecondary education.
retrieval_query: completed first four years of postsecondary education American opportunity credit
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: At the end of 2025, did you have a federal or state felony conviction for possessing or distributing a controlled substance?
why_ask: This is one of the four eligibility questions for the American opportunity credit; the answer stays in the file for the preparer.
retrieval_query: felony drug conviction American opportunity credit
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Did you pay for books, supplies or equipment that your courses required?
why_ask: Required course materials count as qualified expenses for the American opportunity credit even when bought outside the school.
retrieval_query: course materials books supplies equipment American opportunity credit qualified expenses
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Did you receive money from a 529 plan or Coverdell education savings account in 2025 (Form 1099-Q)?
why_ask: Distributions must be matched against qualified expenses and credits; taxable distributions are outside the volunteer scope.
retrieval_query: Form 1099-Q qualified tuition program distribution coordination with education credits
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab J, Education Benefits (structure only)

question: Did you have a green card (lawful permanent resident status) at any time in 2025?
why_ask: A green card holder is a resident alien for tax purposes and is taxed like a U.S. citizen; Form 8843 is for nonimmigrant visa holders.
retrieval_query: lawful permanent resident green card test resident alien
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab L, Substantial Presence Test Decision Chart 1 (Student) (structure only); Resident or Nonresident Alien Decision Tree step 1

question: What visa were you in the U.S. on as a student in 2025: F, J, M, Q, or another visa?
why_ask: Students on F, J, M or Q visas can be exempt individuals whose days do not count for the substantial presence test (Form 8843, Part I line 1a and Part III).
retrieval_query: exempt individual student F J M Q visa days not counted substantial presence test
origin: IRS Form 8843 (2025) Part I line 1a, Part III; Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab L, Substantial Presence Test Decision Chart 1 (Student) (structure only)

question: Did you follow the requirements of your student visa during 2025 (for example full-time enrollment and authorized work only)?
why_ask: Days can be excluded as an exempt student only if the student substantially complied with the visa requirements (Pub 4012 Tab L, step 2).
retrieval_query: student exempt individual substantially complied with visa requirements
origin: Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab L, Substantial Presence Test Decision Chart 1 (Student) (structure only), step 2

question: Counting 2025, were you in the U.S. as a student, teacher or trainee (F, J, M or Q visa) during any part of more than 5 calendar years?
why_ask: A student stops being an exempt individual after 5 calendar years unless an exception applies (Form 8843, Part III line 12).
retrieval_query: student exempt for more than 5 calendar years Form 8843 line 12
origin: IRS Form 8843 (2025) Part III line 12; Pub 4012 (Rev. 10-2026) Tab L, Substantial Presence Test Decision Chart 1 (Student) (structure only), step 3

question: During 2025, did you apply for, or take other steps toward, a green card (lawful permanent resident status)?
why_ask: Steps toward permanent residence are asked on Form 8843 (Part III line 13) and can stop days from being excluded.
retrieval_query: applied for lawful permanent resident status Form 8843 student
